title: 第二十二章 藤迹
content_zh:
日子在石室里，再次被切割成固定的、缓慢的片段。

    晨起（以岩缝天光为凭），饮用掺了凝露果汁液和木铃兰碎末的温水，苦涩中带着一丝回甘，清凉润泽，仿佛能洗净一夜沉疴带来的滞涩。然后，是苏芸检查伤口、换药。伤口愈合的速度依旧慢得令人心焦，但新生的肉芽已将那可怕的裂口填平了大半，颜色也从暗红转为浅粉，只是边缘仍有些红肿，触碰时痛感清晰。敷上苏芸用定魂草、断续藤根须和几种陈默不认识的草药新调配的药膏，带来一种混合了清凉、微麻和温养的复杂感觉。

    换药后，苏芸会指导陈默练习那套新推演的行气法。不再是讲述，而是修正。陈默按照前一日的方法，以四肢末端为引，尝试捕捉、引导外界那稀薄的水木灵气。每一次尝试，都如同在浓雾中摸索，在干涸的河床上挖掘，艰难而笨拙。他能引动的灵气丝缕微弱，运行路径模糊难辨，时常“走失”或“消散”，甚至在流经某些被火毒盘踞的经脉节点时，会引起剧烈的灼痛反噬，疼得他冷汗涔涔，几欲中断。

    苏芸便在一旁，观察他的呼吸、神色、身体细微的颤动。在他气息紊乱、路径偏离时，会及时出声提醒，或用手指虚点他身体某处，示意气机滞涩或偏离的位置。在他因火毒反噬而痛苦不堪时，会让他立刻停止，引导他运转那套基础的呼吸法，平复躁动的气血和灵气，待稳定后，再尝试从其他路径绕行，或干脆在那个节点前停下，只做温养，不做冲击。

    “莫要强求。此法非为克敌，只为调和。火毒如淤塞之顽石，你以柔弱之水、初生之木去冲刷，急不得。今日能引一丝灵气，浸润一寸干裂之土，便是进益。明日再浸一寸，日积月累，顽石或可松动，干土或可回润。”苏芸的声音总是平静，带着一种不容置疑的说服力，驱散着陈默因进展缓慢而生的焦躁和自我怀疑。

    练习半个时辰，无论有无明显收获，苏芸都会让他停下。然后，是进食。食物很简单，多是苏芸从石室附近采集的野菜、菌菇（她极为谨慎，只选取确认无毒的几种），加上偶尔小荷在更外围安全区域设下的简单陷阱捕获的小型山鼠或飞鸟，用陶罐混着清水和少许盐粒（苏芸随身带的，不多）煮成一锅浓淡不一的汤。滋味寡淡，但能果腹，补充体力。苏芸似乎对食物的要求极低，吃得很少，却将大部分肉食和营养好些的部分，分给重伤的陈默和正在长身体的小荷。

    午后，是苏芸辨识、处理草药的时辰。她会将小荷带回来的、或她自己新采集的各种草药，在石室门口透光稍好处摊开，一一讲解。这次，不止是教陈默，也似乎有意无意地，让缩在角落的小荷旁听。

    “这是‘蛇衔草’，叶如蛇信，有剧毒，但取其根部汁液，以特殊手法炮制，可解数种蛇毒，是炼制低阶解毒丹的辅药之一。但炮制不当，便是致命毒药。采摘时需戴手套，避免汁液沾染皮肤。”

    “这是‘地锦’，攀附岩石而生，叶片小而密，秋季变红。其茎叶煎水，有微弱止血收敛之效，对普通外伤可用，但于你等深入筋骨的火毒刀剑之伤，效用甚微。辨识时，需注意与另一种有毒的‘爬山虎’区分，后者叶缘有细齿，汁液乳白，沾之红肿……”

    “这是‘鬼灯笼’，果实如小灯笼，未熟时青绿，成熟后艳红，有微弱致幻毒性，不可食用。但其根茎，埋土三年以上者，挖出阴干，研磨成粉，可作低阶迷魂香的原料，亦可用于某些特殊丹药的催化……”

    苏芸的讲解，不再局限于草药本身的形态、药性，开始涉及更多：生长环境的细微差异对药性的影响，不同采摘时令导致的药力变化，简易的炮制手法（晒、阴、焙、蒸、煮）及其原理，甚至是一些基础的、低阶丹药的配伍思路和禁忌。她讲得依旧条理清晰，但内容明显深了许多，常常让陈默需要反复咀嚼，才能理解其中关窍。小荷更是听得云里雾里，大眼睛里满是懵懂，但依然努力地听着、记着。

    陈默如饥似渴地吸收着这些知识。他拿出那本周安笔记，对照着苏芸的讲解，发现自己之前的理解是何等粗陋浅薄。许多笔记上语焉不详或一笔带过的地方，在苏芸这里得到了透彻的阐释；而笔记上某些看似“经验之谈”的做法，在苏芸的体系下，被指出了隐患和谬误。他不再仅仅死记硬背，开始尝试理解背后的“理”，比如为何水属性灵气能润下化解，木属性灵气能生发疏泄，不同属性的草药配伍会产生何种相生相克的变化。

    苏芸似乎也乐见他这种主动的思考。在他提出一些略显稚嫩却切中要害的问题时，她会多解释几句，眼中偶尔会闪过一丝几不可察的、类似赞许的神色。但大多数时候，她依旧是那副清冷平静的模样，仿佛只是在完成一项既定的教学任务。

    辨认、讲解完草药，苏芸会让小荷帮忙处理一些简单的清洗、晾晒工作，她自己则开始用那些处理好的药材，调配新的药膏，或熬制给陈默内服的汤药。她似乎对药性的把握和剂量的拿捏，有着近乎直觉般的精准。每一次调整方子，都会向陈默说明缘由——因他伤势恢复到了某个阶段，因体内火毒出现了某种变化，或因近日天气转阴、瘴气略重需加强化毒之力等等。

    陈默的伤势，在这种细致入微、量身定制的调理下，以一种虽然缓慢、却稳定得令人心安的步伐，一点点好转。左胸伤口终于完全愈合，留下一道狰狞的、暗红色的扭曲疤痕，触摸时仍有些僵硬和隐痛，但已不影响基本的活动。体内的火毒，在持续的药力化解和行气法疏导下，明显被压制、驱散了许多。虽然依旧盘踞在几条主要经脉的深处，带来持续的灼痛和运行时的滞涩，但已不再像最初那样疯狂肆虐，让他时刻处于生死边缘。他的脸色不再那么苍白得吓人，呼吸也日渐平稳有力。

    他开始能在苏芸的搀扶下，慢慢走出石室，在洞口附近那片被藤蔓半遮掩的空地上，晒一小会儿太阳。阳光透过稀疏的枝叶和淡薄的瘴气，洒在身上，暖洋洋的，带着山林特有的、被草木过滤后的清新气息，让他有种恍如隔世之感。他看着石缝外那一片幽深的、仿佛亘古不变的绿色，听着远处隐约的鸟鸣和溪流声，第一次如此清晰地感受到“活着”的实感，也感受到自身与这片危险而又蕴藏生机的山林之间，那种微妙而复杂的联系。

    小荷的变化也很明显。最初的惊恐和麻木渐渐褪去，虽然眼神里依旧藏着深深的后怕和对苏芸的敬畏，但行动间已利落了许多。她似乎将这份“收留”和“教授”视为天大的恩情，不仅将苏芸交代的活计做得一丝不苟，还会主动去更远些（但绝不超过苏芸划定的安全线）的地方采集野菜、捡拾柴火，甚至尝试用苏芸教的简单方法，设置更精巧的陷阱。她依旧很少说话，但看向陈默的眼神里，感激和愧疚之色日浓。偶尔，她会在苏芸教授草药时，鼓起勇气提出一两个极其简单的问题，苏芸也会简短地回答。

    石室里的气氛，在日复一日的养伤、修炼、辨识草药、准备食物的循环中，变得奇异而稳定。三人之间，没有多少言语交流，却形成了一种基于生存和当前共同目标的、沉默的默契。苏芸是主导者、传授者、医者。陈默是伤者、学习者、被保护者。小荷是助手、劳力、被收留者。各自守着自己的位置，完成分内之事，维持着这方狭小天地脆弱的平衡。

    然而，平静之下，暗流从未止息。

    苏芸的警戒，从未放松。她每日都会在固定时辰，独自外出约莫一炷香时间，沿着石室周围仔细探查，检查是否有外人或野兽靠近的痕迹，也顺手补充一些必需品。她的脸色总是凝重，回来后会沉默许久。陈默注意到，她带回来的食物和草药，品质似乎在缓慢下降，种类也在减少。有一次，她甚至带回了一小块沾着暗红色污迹、似乎是某种兽皮的碎片，在篝火边翻看了很久，眉头紧锁。

    是赵明他们还在附近搜寻？还是黑风涧深处又发生了什么变故？抑或是，宗门已经发现了王炎的失踪，开始调查？

    陈默没有问。他知道，问了苏芸也未必会说，徒增烦恼。他只能将这份隐忧压在心底，转化为更专注的修炼和恢复。他需要尽快好起来，拥有至少自保的能力，而不是永远做一个拖累。

    他开始尝试在苏芸的指导下，进行一些极轻微的、不牵动左胸旧伤的肢体活动。不是体术残篇里那些高难度的动作，只是最简单的伸展、缓慢的深蹲、倚着岩壁的轻微靠墙静立。每一次，都伴随着肌肉的酸痛和伤处的隐痛，但他坚持着。他感觉，随着身体活动增加，气血运行似乎加快了些，对那套行气法的练习，也似乎顺利了一分。

    这日傍晚，苏芸检查完陈默当日的行气练习，又为他换了药，忽然道：“你体内火毒，已化去近半，残余多盘踞于手厥阴心包经、手少阳三焦经等数条主脉交会之处，顽固异常。单靠药力与行气法疏导，恐需极长时间，且易留隐患。”

    陈默心中一凛，看向苏芸。

    “我思忖数日，或有一法，可试。”苏芸从怀里拿出一个小巧的、用软木塞紧的竹筒，不过手指长短。“此乃我以‘银线鲵’脊骨髓液，混合‘寒烟草’、‘透骨草’精华，佐以数味辅药，炼制而成的‘寒髓液’。性极寒，有冻结、化散异种灵力、疏通淤塞经脉之奇效，尤其针对火毒、炎煞等阳毒。但……药性猛烈，且银线鲵髓液本身蕴含微弱水毒，使用不当，反易寒毒入体，损伤经脉根本。”

    她将竹筒递给陈默，神色严肃：“用法是，取一滴，置于掌心，以内息化开，涂抹于火毒盘踞最盛的穴位附近，如‘劳宫’、‘内关’、‘膻中’等处，配合行气法，徐徐导引其寒力，渗入经脉，与火毒相激相化。过程极为痛苦，且需精确控制药力渗透的深浅与范围，稍有差池，便可能寒热相冲，经脉崩裂，或寒毒侵体，留下难以治愈的寒症。”
content_en:
The days in the stone room were once again cut into fixed and slow fragments.
When you get up in the morning (based on the skylight in the rock crevices), drink warm water mixed with dew juice juice and mulberry powder. It is bitter with a hint of sweetness, cool and moist, and seems to be able to wash away the stagnation caused by a night of illness.Then, Su Yun checked the wound and changed the dressing.The healing speed of the wound is still worryingly slow, but the new granulation has filled up most of the terrible gap, and the color has also changed from dark red to light pink, but there is still some redness and swelling at the edges, and the pain is clearly felt when touched.Applying Su Yun's newly prepared ointment using Soul-fixing Grass, Dipsus Vine roots and several herbs that Chen Mo didn't recognize brought a complex feeling of coolness, slight numbness and warmth.
After changing the dressing, Su Yun will guide Chen Mo to practice the newly deduced qi-moving method.No longer telling, but correcting.Chen Mo followed the method from the previous day, using the ends of his limbs as guides to try to capture and guide the thin water and wood aura from the outside world.Every attempt was like groping in thick fog or digging on a dry river bed, difficult and clumsy.The spiritual energy he could activate was weak, and its path was blurry and difficult to discern. It often "lost" or "dissipated." Even when it flowed through certain meridians that were entangled with fire poison, it would cause severe burning pain, causing him to break out in cold sweat and almost want to stop.
Su Yun stood aside, observing his breathing, expression, and subtle tremors of his body.When his breath is disordered or his path deviates, he will sound a reminder in time, or point his finger somewhere on his body to indicate where his qi is stagnant or deviated.When he is in extreme pain due to the backlash of fire poison, he will be asked to stop immediately, and he will be guided to use the basic breathing method to calm the restless Qi, blood and spiritual energy. After stabilizing, he will try to detour through other paths, or simply stop in front of that node, only to warm up and not to impact.
"Don't force it. This method is not to defeat the enemy, but to reconcile it. The poison of fire is like a stubborn stone blocked by siltation. You can wash it away with soft water and young trees. There is no rush. If you can draw a trace of spiritual energy today and soak an inch of dry and cracked soil, it is a benefit. Ming.With each passing day, stubborn rocks may be loosened, and dry soil may be moisturized." Su Yun's voice was always calm, with an unquestionable persuasiveness, dispelling Chen Mo's anxiety and self-doubt caused by the slow progress.
After practicing for half an hour, Su Yun would ask him to stop regardless of whether there was any obvious gain or not.Then, there’s eating.The food was very simple, mostly wild vegetables and mushrooms collected by Su Yun from near the stone chamber (she was extremely cautious and only selected a few types that were confirmed to be non-toxic), plus occasionally small mountain rats or birds caught in simple traps set by Xiao He in the outer safety area. They were mixed with water and a little salt in a clay pot (not much that Su Yun brought with her) to cook a pot of soup of different thicknesses.The taste is bland, but it can satisfy your hunger and replenish your physical strength.Su Yun seemed to have very low requirements for food. She ate very little, but gave most of the meat and more nutritious parts to the seriously injured Chen Mo and the growing Xiao He.
In the afternoon, it is Su Yun's time to identify and process herbs.She would spread out various herbs brought back by Xiaohe or newly collected by herself at the door of the stone room where the light was better, and explain them one by one.This time, he not only taught Chen Mo, but also let Xiao He, who was huddled in the corner, listen, intentionally or unintentionally.
"This is 'Snake Grass'. Its leaves are like snake letters and it is highly poisonous. However, the juice from its roots is prepared using special techniques. It can detoxify several kinds of snake venom. It is one of the auxiliary drugs for refining low-level detoxification pills. However, if it is not prepared properly, it will be a fatal poison. You need to wear gloves when picking to prevent the juice from contaminating the skin."
"This is 'Dijin', which grows on rocks. Its leaves are small and dense, and turn red in autumn. Its stems and leaves are boiled in water, which has a weak hemostasis and astringent effect. It can be used for ordinary trauma, but it has little effect on injuries caused by fire poison swords that penetrate deep into the bones. When identifying, you need to pay attention to distinguish it from another poisonous 'creeper'. The latter has fine teeth on the leaf edge, milky white sap, and redness and swelling..."
"This is a 'ghost lantern'. The fruit is like a small lantern. It is green when unripe and bright red when ripe. It has weak hallucinogenic toxicity and is not edible. However, its rhizome, if buried in the soil for more than three years, can be dug out, dried in the shade, and ground into powder. It can be used as a raw material for low-level ecstasy incense, and can also be used to catalyze some special elixirs..."
Su Yun's explanation was no longer limited to the form and medicinal properties of the herbs themselves, but began to cover more: the influence of subtle differences in the growth environment on the medicinal properties, the changes in medicinal potency caused by different picking seasons, simple processing techniques (sun, shade, roasting, steaming, boiling) and their principles, and even the compatibility ideas and taboos of some basic, low-level elixirs.She still spoke clearly and coherently, but the content was obviously much deeper. Chen Mo often had to chew over it repeatedly before he could understand the key points.Xiao He was even more confused when he heard it, and his big eyes were full of confusion, but he still tried hard to listen and remember.
Chen Mo absorbed this knowledge eagerly.He took out his Zhou An notebook and compared it with Su Yun's explanation, and found out how crude and shallow his previous understanding was.Many of the things that were unclear or passed over in the notes were thoroughly explained by Su Yun; and some practices that seemed to be "speaking from experience" in the notes were pointed out hidden dangers and fallacies under Su Yun's system.He no longer just memorized it by rote, but began to try to understand the "principle" behind it, such as why water-attribute spiritual energy can moisturize and dissolve, wood-attribute spiritual energy can generate hair, and what kind of mutually reinforcing changes will occur when the compatibility of herbs with different attributes will occur.
Su Yun seemed to be happy to see his proactive thinking.When he asked some slightly naive but to-the-point questions, she would explain a few more words, and occasionally there would be an almost imperceptible look of approval in her eyes.But most of the time, she still looks cool and calm, as if she is just completing an established teaching task.
After identifying and explaining the herbs, Su Yun asked Xiao He to help with some simple cleaning and drying tasks, while she herself began to use the prepared herbs to prepare new ointments or brew decoctions for Chen Mo to take internally.She seems to have an almost intuitive precision in grasping the properties of the medicine and the dosage.Every time the prescription is adjusted, the reason will be explained to Chen Mo - because his injury has recovered to a certain stage, because there has been some change in the fire poison in the body, or because the weather has turned cloudy recently and the miasma has become slightly heavier, and the power of the poison needs to be strengthened, etc.
Under this meticulous and tailor-made treatment, Chen Mo's injury improved little by little at a slow but steady pace that was reassuring.The wound on the left chest finally healed completely, leaving behind a hideous, dark red twisted scar. It was still stiff and painful when touched, but it no longer affected basic activities.The fire poison in the body was obviously suppressed and dispersed a lot with the continuous use of medicinal power and Qi-moving methods.Although it was still entrenched in the depths of several major meridians, causing continuous burning pain and sluggishness during operation, it was no longer as crazy and raging as it was at the beginning, leaving him always on the edge of life and death.His face was no longer so frighteningly pale, and his breathing was becoming smoother and stronger.
He began to be able to slowly walk out of the stone room with Su Yun's support, and basked in the sun for a short while in the open space half-covered by vines near the entrance of the cave.The sun shone on his body through the sparse branches and leaves and the faint miasma. It was warm and brought with it the fresh breath filtered by the vegetation that was unique to the mountain forest, making him feel as if he was in another world.He looked at the deep, seemingly eternal green outside the stone crevices, and listened to the faint chirping of birds and streams in the distance. For the first time, he felt the real sense of "alive" so clearly, and he also felt the subtle and complex connection between himself and this dangerous yet vital mountain forest.
The changes in Xiaohe are also obvious.The initial panic and numbness gradually faded away. Although there was still deep fear and awe for Su Yun in his eyes, his actions were much more agile.She seemed to regard this "taking in" and "professing" as a great favor. Not only did she do the tasks given by Su Yun meticulously, she would also take the initiative to go further (but never beyond the safety line drawn by Su Yun) to collect wild vegetables and firewood, and even tried to use the simple methods taught by Su Yun to set more elaborate traps.She still rarely spoke, but the look in her eyes that looked at Chen Mo became increasingly filled with gratitude and guilt.Occasionally, when Su Yun was teaching herbal medicine, she would summon up the courage to ask one or two extremely simple questions, and Su Yun would answer briefly.
The atmosphere in the stone room became strange and stable during the day-to-day cycle of recuperating, practicing, identifying herbs, and preparing food.There was not much verbal communication between the three of them, but a silent understanding based on survival and current common goals was formed.Su Yun is a leader, a teacher, and a healer.Chen Mo is the injured, the learner, and the protected.Xiaohe is an assistant, a laborer, and a shelter.Each holds their own position, completes their duties, and maintains the fragile balance of this small world.
However, under the calm, the undercurrent never stops.
Su Yun's vigilance never relaxed.She would go out alone at a fixed time every day for about a stick of incense, and carefully explore around the stone chamber to check if there were any signs of approaching outsiders or wild animals, and also replenish some necessities.Her face is always solemn and she will be silent for a long time after coming back.Chen Mo noticed that the quality of the food and herbs she brought back seemed to be slowly declining, and the types were also decreasing.Once, she even brought back a small fragment with dark red stains that seemed to be some kind of animal skin. She looked at it beside the campfire for a long time, frowning.
Is it Zhao Ming and the others who are still searching nearby?Or is something else happening deep in the Black Wind Stream?Or has the sect discovered Wang Yan's disappearance and started investigating?
